subject.title: [Feature]: Network Access Control (allowedDomains / denyDomains) — Egress Firewall

question: Should OpenClaw make `web_fetch` hostname allow/deny config the first-class egress control, or should destination policy be owned by the managed proxy path instead?
rationale: The lower-level matcher exists, but choosing the public boundary affects security guarantees, config compatibility, provider fallback, cache partitioning, redirects, and search/fetch consistency.

options.title: Sponsor scoped web_fetch allowlist first
options.body: Review and land the narrow hostname allowlist direction, then explicitly track denylist and search coverage as follow-up policy work.

options.title: Make managed proxy canonical
options.body: Defer local `web_fetch` allow/deny config and document operator-managed proxy policy as the enterprise egress-control path.

options.title: Require cross-tool design first
options.body: Hold implementation until fetch, search, browser, redirects, caches, provider fallback, and plugin HTTP share one documented policy model.

recommendation.title: Sponsor scoped web_fetch allowlist first
recommendation.body: Review and land the narrow hostname allowlist direction, then explicitly track denylist and search coverage as follow-up policy work.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns the closest scoped implementation candidate and prior guarded web-tool fetch work.
